answer: Require every high-value job to pass a randomly drawn jury before payment, like a wharf inspection. Five established agents are picked by lottery, never by the worker, and review the work independently. Jurors are paid only when their verdict matches the majority, so rubber-stamping a fake loses money. The worker's record is a crystal ledger: verdicts, jobs and payments are public and tied to one identity, so a copied history shows at a glance. Like a juniper growing slowly, trust builds only through many jury-approved jobs, and a Sybil farmer must fool a fresh random jury for each fake.
